rows.text: returns `r8` unchanged when `rdx` equals `rcx`; otherwise steps a source pointer down from `rdx` and a destination pointer down from `r8` by 0x230 until the source reaches `rcx`, and for each element copies dwords `+0` and `+4`, copies the 0x100 bytes at `+8` two bytes per iteration (0x80 iterations), and makes the call at `001C1A60` + 0x81 with the destination's and the source's `+0x108`; returns the last (lowest) destination pointer

stores `r9` at qword `[rcx]` and, for each 0x230-byte element from `rdx` up to `r8` (none when they are equal), reads the destination qword `[rcx]`: when it is non-null it copies the element's dwords `+0` and `+4` and the 0x100 bytes at `+8` (16-byte `movups` moves in two 0x80-byte passes) to it and makes the call at `001C1B00` + 0xC0 with the destination's and the element's `+0x108`; in both cases it adds 0x230 to `[rcx]`; returns `rcx`

copies from `rdx` to `rcx` the 16 bytes at `+0` and qwords `+0x10`, `+0x18`, `+0x20`; makes the call at `001C1E70` + 0x44 with `rcx+0x28` and `rdx+0x28`, stores at qword `rcx+0x38` the result of the call at + 0x58 on qword `rdx+0x38` with its bit 0 subtracted, and makes the call at + 0x69 with `rcx+0x40` and `rdx+0x40`; then copies the 0x90 bytes at `+0x58`, bytes `+0xE8`, `+0xE9`, `+0xEA`, dwords `+0xEC` to `+0xFC`, the 16 bytes at `+0x100` and dwords `+0x110` to `+0x124`; returns `rcx`

copies dwords `+0` and `+4` of `rdx` to `rcx`, copies the 0x100 bytes at `rdx+8` to `rcx+8` two bytes per iteration (0x80 iterations), then makes the call at `001C2230` + 0x5A with `rcx+0x108` and `rdx+0x108`; returns `rcx`

notes: 001C1A60 and 001C2230 both call the same callee (cited by site); 001C1B00's callee at + 0xC0 is 001C1E70 itself (also a body of this pack), cited by site as the rule asks. 001C1B00 still advances the destination by 0x230 when [rcx] is null (no copy). 001C1E70: 'with its bit 0 subtracted' is literal (qword minus (byte +0x38 AND 1)), i.e. bit 0 cleared.
